proposal.hypothesis: 128-thread groups processing two rows with parameter vectors cached in registers and simd_sum reduction should cut barrier and repeated parameter traffic versus the 256-thread barrier-tree incumbent.

256-thread groups processing 4 rows reuse cached FP32 weights across 4 rows, halve register-held vectors per row, and use only 2 barriers per row, cutting weight traffic and spill pressure versus the 128-thread 2-row incumbent.
128-bit uint4 loads/stores with 256-thread groups processing 4 rows and caching parameters in registers reduce instruction and barrier overhead versus 64-bit half4 2-row schedule.
